items.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998
items.q: I stayed 2-2-1/2 years, almost 3 years with Earl.

ctx.x: And you worked on and off with him in later years too.

Yeah. Well we happened to be thrown into the same theater at the same time, but I never was with the band anymore. But we were in Chicago later, after I had “Don’t Go To Strangers,” and we worked together and he was so happy for me, because he was an extremely nice man. I happened to have very nice bosses. Because Earl Hines was wonderful, and J.C. Heard was a wonderful boss for me.
That’s fortunate because it could have gone the other way.

items.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998
items.q: Etta has collaborated with such greats as ... Earl “Fatha” Hines ... both in concert and on recordings.

ctx.x: Song-stylist Etta Jones grew up in New York City and began her singing career as a teenager in Buddy Johnson’s band. Since then Etta has collaborated with such greats as J.C. Heard, Oliver Nelson, Earl “Fatha” Hines, Jack McDuff, Kenny Burrell, Cedar Walton and many others, both in concert and on recordings. She has toured Europe and Asia, and has recorded for RCA Victor, Jubilee, Prestige, Muse and HighNote Records. Etta was interviewed in Clinton, New York on October 2, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
